claims.claim: NYCE Payments Network, LLC is an FIS company; the network's own e-book describes it as more than 30 years old.
claims.quote: NYCE Payments Network®, LLC (NYCE), an FIS™ company, is the strongest network partner
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: PDF footer '©2023 FIS'; document code 2318479. Read with pypdf after WebFetch saved the binary.

claims.claim: FIS, NYCE's parent, is headquartered at 347 Riverside Avenue, Jacksonville, Florida (FY2025 10-K); the 10-K text does not mention NYCE by name.
claims.quote: FIS' corporate headquarters is located at 347 Riverside Avenue, Jacksonville, Florida.
claims.title: Form 10-K, Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Grep of the full 10-K text for 'NYCE', 'debit network', 'PIN debit', 'Regulation II' and 'Durbin' returned zero hits.

claims.claim: The Digital Transactions buyers' guide lists NYCE Payments Network, LLC at a Secaucus, New Jersey address with FIS's Jacksonville main phone number.
claims.quote: 401 Plaza Drive - 2nd Floor, Secaucus, NJ 7094, United States
claims.title: NYCE Payments Network, LLC - Buyers Guide
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: Listing shows phone +1 904-438-6000, which is FIS's registrant phone in the 10-K. Page shows date 2024-10-07 in search results.

claims.claim: Ownership change: on January 9, 2026 FIS completed the purchase of Global Payments' Issuer Solutions business and sold its remaining Worldpay stake, under agreements signed April 17, 2025.
claims.quote: On January 9, 2026, Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., a Georgia corporation (“FIS”) completed its previously announced (i) acquisition of the Issuer Solutions business
claims.title: Form 8-K, Item 2.01 Completion of Acquisition or Disposition of Assets
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: NYCE itself did not change hands; it remains inside FIS. FIS paid approximately $7.7 billion in cash plus its Worldpay interest.

claims.claim: Ownership context: FIS sold a 55% interest in Worldpay Merchant Solutions to GTCR on January 31, 2024, keeping NYCE inside FIS's Banking segment.
claims.quote: On January 31, 2024, we completed the sale (the "2024 Worldpay Sale") of a 55% equity interest in our Worldpay Merchant Solutions business
claims.title: Form 10-K, Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: NYCE's cardholder site claims acceptance at over 90% of U.S. ATMs and more than 2 million retail locations.
claims.quote: Your debit card works at over 90% of ATMs in the U.S. thanks to the NYCE® Payments Network
claims.title: NYCE - cardholder site
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Same page: 'Pay at more than 2 million retail locations across the U.S.' No date on page; no card, participant or transaction counts anywhere on public FIS/NYCE pages.

claims.claim: NYCE is classified by the Federal Reserve as a single-message network in its Regulation II interchange data.
claims.quote: Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.title: Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page notes 'Data revised as of June 10, 2025'; NYCE appears under single-message networks for 2024.

claims.claim: NYCE states it connects to every major EFT processor in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, and its e-book says cardholders get military-base ATM access via AFFN.
claims.quote: connects to every major EFT processor in the U.S. and Puerto Rico
claims.title: NYCE Payments Network | FIS
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: E-book adds: 'access to ATMs at U.S. military bases worldwide through NYCE's partnership with AFFN®'.

claims.claim: Brand family: FIS positions NYCE for banks and CULIANCE for credit unions as its two debit payments networks.
claims.quote: For banks of all sizes, we provide NYCE® Payments Network, which gives customers secure, real-time access to their money
claims.title: Move money to make money with your debit payments network (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Same page: 'through CULIANCE®, we do the same for credit unions, offering the country's largest surcharge-free ATM network'. Figures are 'thousands of ATM and millions of point-of-sale (POS) locations' -- vaguer than nyce.net's 90%/2 million.

claims.claim: Issuer catalogue (core): PIN and PINless POS, eCommerce, On-Demand Payments (bill pay, account funding, rebates/refunds, A2A/B2B/B2C/P2P), ATM access, stand-in processing.
claims.quote: NYCE On-Demand Payments are a comprehensive family of “card not present” transactions that facilitate the electronification of payments
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Also lists Direct Bill Payment, Account Funding, Rebates and Refunds, A2A, B2B, B2C and P2P Transfers as interchange-earning categories for issuers.

claims.claim: Fraud and risk (value-added, via FICO): Risk Monitoring Service with Falcon scores, FICO Card Alert Service, iCVx Verification and Authorization Blocking.
claims.quote: Risk Monitoring Service (RMS), created in association with FICO, and the FICO® Card Alert Service.
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: RMS 'analyzes incoming transactions ... using three, unique Falcon Fraud scores'; scores can be delivered to the issuer's EFT processor.

claims.claim: ATM services (optional programmes): SUM surcharge-free with per-transaction pricing, no-cost Shared Deposit ATMs, Gateway Service to other surcharge-free networks with single settlement.
claims.quote: SUM is distinguished by its per transaction pricing and flexible ATM participation options.
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Gateway Service: 'a single online interface and single point settlement'. Shared Deposit: 'Enroll in this no-cost program'.

claims.claim: Faster payments and tokenisation: NYCE claims first U.S. domestic debit network live with tokenized transactions and operates PayNet, used by FIS People Pay and Zelle.
claims.quote: First U.S. domestic debit network to go live with tokenized transactions
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: 'Launched PayNet®, the faster payments network that supports P2P solutions such as FIS People Pay and Early Warning's Zelle®'. Also cites an Amazon FI-branded checkout collaboration.

claims.claim: Merchant/acquirer offer: Smart Basket is an FIS item-level offers network that pairs with NYCE routing to lower acceptance costs and stack promotions.
claims.quote: NYCE® Payments Network delivers smart routing and resilient transaction processing to reduce acceptance costs
claims.title: Smart Basket | FIS
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Audiences named on page: issuers, merchants, brands/CPGs. CTAs: Contact us, Request a demo, Get pricing, Read e-book.

claims.claim: Authorisation optimisation: FIS says a dedicated team monitors auth rates for issuers, acquirers and merchants and fixes MCC/message errors.
claims.quote: a dedicated and expert team at FIS constantly monitors authorization rates for debit card issuers, acquirers and merchants
claims.title: Move money to make money with your debit payments network (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Case claims: MCC correction gave a merchant '20% increase in auth rate'; an acquirer got '240,000 extra new approvals over the next 30 days'.

claims.claim: The only partner-facing marketing property is the FIS product page; its CTAs route to a contact form and the gated FIS Client Portal (my.fisglobal.com) rather than any NYCE-specific portal.
claims.quote: Empower debit cardholders with secure, real-time payments and ATM access
claims.title: NYCE Payments Network | FIS
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Links found: nyce.net (cardholder), Smart Basket, fisglobal.com/solutions-contact (Contact us / Request a demo / Get pricing), my.fisglobal.com/app/login (Client Portal, returns HTTP 403 to curl), three e-book PDFs.

claims.claim: nyce.net is a cardholder-only site (ATM locators, FAQs) that refers cardholders to their bank and links back to the FIS product page for institutions.
claims.quote: Contact your financial institution directly — they can confirm your card's participation in the NYCE network
claims.title: NYCE FAQs
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Site links: atmlocator/nyce.html, atmlocator/sum.html, faqs.html, fisglobal.com product page, FIS privacy and terms.

claims.claim: FIS's public developer portal (developer.fisglobal.com redirects to Code Connect) is a JavaScript app whose HTML exposes no NYCE, debit network, PayNet or ATM API; no NYCE developer reference is readable logged out.
claims.quote: Code Connect: API Marketplace | FIS
claims.title: Code Connect: API Marketplace | FIS
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: Only the page title was renderable; product count, auth scheme, sandbox, SDKs, webhooks, versioning and rate limits for NYCE are not found publicly.

claims.claim: Onboarding as published is issuer-side via the existing EFT processor with no card reissue; no membership types, application steps, fees or certification stages are published.
claims.quote: No need to reissue debit cards • Interfaces with your EFT processor • Minimal implementation tasks for your staff
claims.title: Move money to make money with your debit payments network (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: 2023 e-book: 'NYCE already connects to every financial institution processor in the U.S. and Puerto Rico, streamlining the implementation process'.

claims.claim: Federal Reserve data for 2024 put NYCE's average interchange at $0.27 per transaction (0.61% of value) across all transactions, and $0.24 (0.48%) for covered transactions.
claims.quote: Data revised as of June 10, 2025
claims.title: Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Exempt: $0.28 / 0.67%; covered: $0.24 / 0.48%; all: $0.27 / 0.61%, per the NYCE row as extracted by WebFetch. Regulator figures, not a published NYCE fee schedule.

claims.claim: Regulator finding for 2023: covered transactions on single-message networks (NYCE's class) averaged $0.24 interchange versus $0.22 on dual-message networks, across 13 networks surveyed.
claims.quote: the average interchange fee for covered transactions processed over single-message networks was $0.24
claims.title: 2023 Interchange Fee Revenue, Covered Issuer Costs, and Covered Issuer and Merchant Fraud Losses Related to Debit Card Transactions
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: 'All 13 card networks that processed debit card transactions in 2022 and 2023 completed the survey'. Single-message share of transactions 28.6%.

claims.claim: Regulation II requires at least two unaffiliated networks per debit card and bars inhibiting merchant routing choice; a 2023 Board proposal to lower the cap is listed without a final status.
claims.quote: prohibits all issuers and networks from restricting the number of networks over which debit transactions may be processed to less than two unaffiliated networks
claims.title: Regulation II (Debit Card Interchange Fees and Routing)
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Page links 'Federal Reserve Board requests comment on a proposal to lower the maximum interchange fee' dated October 25, 2023; no adoption date shown.

claims.claim: NYCE publishes no interchange or network fee schedule; its marketing asserts 'industry-leading interchange rates' and low network fees without numbers.
claims.quote: Industry-leading interchange rates on point-of-sale (POS), eCommerce and On-Demand Payments for all charters and sizes
claims.title: Your Strategic Partner in Payments - NYCE Payment Networks (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: No fee tables, effective dates, assessment or cross-border fees on any public FIS/NYCE page fetched.

claims.claim: Support model as published: a dedicated client relations team, an 800 number and a 99.99% transaction-time SLA claim on dual-node architecture.
claims.quote: Dual-node architecture providing redundancy, peace of mind and 100% uptime, exceeding 99.99% transaction time SLAs
claims.title: Move money to make money with your debit payments network (e-book)
claims.label: Vendor
claims.note: 2023 e-book contact: 'CONTACT US 800.822.6758 www.nyce.net' and getinfo@fisglobal.com; 'For more information, please contact your NYCE representative'. No hours, languages or published SLA document.

claims.claim: 2025-04-17: FIS signs agreements to buy Global Payments' Issuer Solutions and sell its Worldpay stake, closing expected in 2026 (closed 2026-01-09).
claims.quote: On April 17, 2025, FIS entered into definitive agreements to (i) buy the Issuer Solutions business
claims.title: Form 10-K, Fidelity National Information Services, Inc., fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Partner relevance: NYCE's parent now also owns the former TSYS issuer processing business, adding an issuer-processor channel alongside the network.
